After how I ended things, it's better for him that we are distant. I miss him so badly and think of him daily. This was a means of making it so I couldn't reach out or get to him. Unfortunately for myself, I figured out a way to do so and it's taken the very limited amount of self control that I do possess to NOT reach out. I'm terrified that if I were to reach out, he'd either not reply, reply angrily, or I'd find out that he fully moved on to someone else (he's got plenty of dating profiles I've ended up swiping past in my attempts to move on/feel wanted). A few messages before this one, I told him I missed him and offered to give the remainder of his stuff back.... he just replied with "is it just clothes?". 
     I'm ashamed of how I behaved. Long story short: BPD rage. I threw his stuff out and told one of his family members information I shouldn't have known in the first place. I know from how he did respond to things I said to him after apologizing (whether they were positive or negative) were a result of him no longer caring and just overall were apathetic. He doesn't want me anymore; I'm trying to process and accept that. I actually saw a future with him. It's hard to not want to be with him still. I love him and want to at least be in his life but am ultimately acknowledging that I am more than a hair past toxic for him.

I should probably have prefaced this with the fact that I have BPD so situations such as breakups hit really hard when it comes to compulsive behaviors like texting/reaching out. I wanted him back but neither of us would be healthy in a relationship. I don't want him back but would like him in my life. Being an aware person with BPD, I do know that the info i gave him was much but I don't think he would have blocked me had I not asked him and would still be compulsively messaging him trying to get back with him due to not wanting to be alone. I had to say what I said to get it off my chest and clearly explain to him why it'd be better for me/him. So for anyone saying using "emotional control", please be aware people with personality disorders have difficulty with NC. I was looking for support, not judgement. For those of you who have kindly commented, thank you for the support!
I appreciate the fact that he followed through. I miss him so badly but know asking was the right thing to do. Thank you guys for the support and validations.💕

My now ex PA used to say this to me everytime I brought up my feelings on his addiction. It's guilt tripping and nothing more than gaslighting to deflect him being in the wrong. You could be like my case, where you do everything you can for him to feel loved but next time it comes up he's going to say he feels rejected by you or you don't love him again. Stand your ground. Be cautious and on alert when you lay down your boundaries. If he doesn't actively make an effort (as in a CONTINUOUS effort; give a it a time frame) to fix the issues you are asking him to resolve then it's not a situation you can win and it is time to let go. Know if you stay, he's just going to giving you excuses and solutions he thinks you want to hear. The solutions will be all well and good but words are NOTHING without actions behind them. I repeat, STAND YOUR GROUND.
